1. (Currently amended) A method comprising: a processor determining that a benefit payment is due to be made to a recipient; the processor accessing a data store containing records of payment transactions made by the recipient; the processor receiving an indication from the data store that the recipient had successfully performed a biometric user authentication with respect to at least one of the payment transactions; the processor accepting the received indication as proof-of-life with respect to the recipient; and the processor making the benefit payment to the recipient in response to said proof-of-life, wherein the method includes a technological solution that applies the proof-of-life verification to a specific technical problem of preventing fraudulent benefit payments by leveraging biometric authentication data from payment transaction systems.

2. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein said at least one payment transaction occurred during a pre-determined period of time prior to said accessing step, and wherein the processor compares timestamps associated with the biometric authentication against a current system timestamp to determine temporal eligibility for benefit payment authorization.

3. (Currently amended) The method of claim 2, wherein said pre-determined period of time is seven days.

4. (Currently amended) The method of claim 2, wherein said pre-determined period of time is 24 hours.

5. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the benefit payment is a social insurance transfer payment and wherein the processor accesses a government benefits database to verify the recipient's eligibility status prior to authorizing payment.

6. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the at least one of the payment transactions includes a credit card account transaction and/or a debit card account transaction, and wherein the processor retrieves biometric authentication records from financial institution servers.

7. (Currently amended) The method of claim 6, wherein a mobile device was used by the recipient to initiate the at least one payment transaction, and wherein the processor accesses biometric authentication logs from the mobile device's secure enclave or trusted execution environment.

8. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the benefit payment is made via an electronic monetary transfer to an account owned by the recipient, and wherein the processor interfaces with a financial network to execute the electronic transfer.

9. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the benefit payment is made by sending a check to the recipient, and wherein the processor generates a check authorization and transmits it to a check printing and mailing system.

10. (Currently amended) A method comprising: a processor determining that a benefit payment is due to be made to a recipient; the processor accessing, at a first point in time, a data store containing records of payment transactions made by the recipient; the processor determining that the data store contains an indication that the recipient had successfully performed a biometric user authentication most recently with respect to one of said payment transactions at a second point in time earlier than the first point in time; the processor comparing a time interval defined by the second and first points in time with a pre-determined permissive time interval; the processor making the benefit payment, without requiring proof-of-life authentication of the recipient, in a case where the time interval defined by the second and first points in time does not exceed the pre-determined permissive time interval; and the processor requiring proof-of-life authentication of the recipient, prior to making the benefit payment, in a case where the time interval defined by the second and first points in time exceeds the pre-determined permissive time interval, wherein the method includes a technological solution that applies temporal-based proof-of-life verification to a specific technical problem of preventing fraudulent benefit payments while reducing authentication burden for recent verified transactions.

11. (Currently amended) The method of claim 10, wherein the pre-determined permissive time interval is seven days, and wherein the processor stores and retrieves the pre-determined permissive time interval from a configuration database.

12. (Currently amended) The method of claim 10, wherein the pre-determined permissive time interval is 24 hours, and wherein the processor calculates elapsed time by subtracting the second point in time from the first point in time using system clock data.

13. (Currently amended) The method of claim 10, wherein the benefit payment is a social insurance transfer payment and wherein the processor accesses a government benefits database to verify the recipient's eligibility status prior to authorizing payment.

14. (Original) An apparatus comprising: a processor; and a memory in communication with the processor, the memory storing program instructions, the processor operative with the program instructions to perform functions as follows: determining that a benefit payment is due to be made to a recipient; accessing a data store containing records of payment transactions made by the recipient; receiving an indication from the data store that the recipient had successfully performed a biometric user authentication with respect to at least one of the payment transactions; accepting the received indication as proof-of-life with respect to the recipient; and making the benefit payment to the recipient in response to said proof-of-life.

15. (Original) The apparatus of claim 14, wherein said at least one payment transaction occurred during a pre-determined period of time prior to said accessing.

16. (Original) The apparatus of claim 15, wherein said pre-determined period of time is seven days.

17. (Original) The apparatus of claim 15, wherein said pre-determined period of time is 24 hours.

18. (Original) The apparatus of claim 14, wherein the benefit payment is a social insurance transfer payment.

19. (Original) The apparatus of claim 14, wherein the at least one of the payment transactions includes a credit card account transaction and/or a debit card account transaction.

20. (Original) The apparatus of claim 19, wherein a mobile device was used by the recipient to initiate the at least one payment transaction.
